children.text: ⬥ Arch-Glacor can be fought in Normal Mode (NM) or Hard Mode (HM)
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• NM can be fought in a group, but HM can only be fought solo
⬥ Arch-Glacor's life points vary based on mode and enrage
slayer assignment applies to NM only
⬥ Arch-Glacor randomly cycles through the 5 mechanics listed below
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Each mechanic can only occur once per cycle, meaning a mechanic can
occur back-to-back if it is the last mechanic of a cycle and the first mechanic of the next
⬥ In NM, mechanics can be toggled on or off to learn the fight, except for Creeping Ice
⬥ In HM, all mechanics are enabled and enrage increases with every kill, with difficulty increasing too
Arch-Glacor primarily uses Magic and Ranged auto-attacks, with stronger style-swapping auto-attacks during
⬥ Pray against the correct attack style
Arch-Glacor becomes immune and summons 4 Glacyte minions. Each minion drops an unstable core on death.
At 250%+ HM enrage, a tougher Bolstered Glacyte also spawns (however, if this is the first mechanic in the fight, this Bolstered Glacyte does
⬥ Use area of effect attacks to clear the minions
⬥ Click the unstable cores only once
Arch-Glacor's auto-attacks hit harder and rotate combat styles, with its Melee hit the strongest.
⬥ Pray against each combat style accordingly
Creeping Ice forces you to one end of the arena, then moving beams cross the arena. Contact with a beam deals heavy damage and stuns you
⬥ Watch the example above for one safe path through the mechanic
⬥ In HM, an additional beam appears after the second beam
Arch-Glacor traps you in the centre of the arena, between its arms. The core deals increasing Magic
⬥ Use strong damaging abilities to break the arm quickly
Creeping Ice traps you at one end of the arena, then Arch-Glacor fires a beam dealing heavy Magic damage. In HM, the beam hits 3 times and the first hit stuns you
⬥ Prioritise blocking the Magic attack(s) with
before the beam in HM to prevent the stun
